title: Complicated feelings on this protest- let’s talk about it #Suffs #Suf...
transcript: Tonight we had yet another Broadway protest, this time at the musical SUFS. SUFS tells the story of the suffragette movement and the passing of the 19th Amendment, which gave white women the right to vote. And tonight, during Act 1, protesters hung this banner from one of the boxes. It says SUFS is a white wash and then links to a website. Now, I went to this website so that you don't have to, and basically here are their claims. So the protesters self identify themselves as an autonomous group of radical, anti racist, queer feminist. They say that CFS claims to teach history, but is really a whitewash, slanted and ultimately dangerous version of history. Now, I do have to say I don't think SUS has ever claimed to teach history or to be 100% historically accurate. And to be honest, I actually think SUS does a better job at acknowledging the racism of the time period than a lot of other history musicals like Hamilton. I'm not gonna sit here and claim it's a perfect show, and it absolutely could go farther on some of these points, but it also doesn't ignore that aspect of history either. They also have a section of the website where you can learn the real story behind stuffs. And to be honest, a lot of the stuff that they point out is already mentioned in the musical. This first paragraph, which talks about how Alice Paul excluded black women from her Party or this paragraph which talked about how black women were asked to march in the back of the march and how Ida B. Wells dissented. They also mentioned Mary Church Tyrell, who chose to march with the black delegation, and her reasons for doing so. And this is also mentioned in the show. And to be clear, none of the information on this website is wrong. In fact, a lot of it is really good information if you want to learn more about this. But I do think calling it the history you won't learn at stuffs feels a little bit disingenuous when a lot of what is on this website is discussed in the show, even if it's not quite at the depth or the level as a lot of people might want. At the end of the day, this is a musical that is condensing decades of history into a two and a half hour narrative, and it is not going to be able to fit everything.
